name: Islamic spherical trigonometry
summary: Islamic scholars used all six functions and proved spherical sine laws and identities.

name: al-Mahani: geometric problems reduced to algebra
summary: Classical construction problems were recast as algebraic (cubic) equations.

name: Ibn al-Haytham and Ibn Sinan: quadrature
summary: Sums of powers were used for areas and volumes, and Archimedean parabola quadrature was generalised.

name: Islamic work on the parallel postulate
summary: Ibn al-Haytham, Khayyam and Tusi studied quadrilaterals as tests of the parallel postulate.

name: al-Karaji: binomial coefficients and early induction
summary: A table of binomial coefficients and stepwise arguments for sums of integers and cubes anticipate induction.

name: al-Karaji polynomial algebra
summary: Algebra was freed from geometric operations, with powers and product rules defined for x and 1/x and polynomial arithmetic.

name: Numerical solution of polynomial equations in China (Ruffini-Horner)
summary: Root-extraction algorithms were extended step by step to cubics and higher-degree polynomial equations.

name: Binomial coefficient triangle in China
summary: A table of binomial coefficients up to the eighth power appeared as the 'ancient method' of expanding powers.

name: Khayyam cubics via conics
summary: Cubics were classified and solved geometrically through intersections of conics, with a claim that ruler and compass are insufficient.

name: Sharaf al-Din al-Tusi
summary: Existence of roots of cubics was analysed through maxima of polynomials.
